simple.meaning: מְעַט (mᵉʻaṭ) is a Hebrew animal word meaning “a little or few (often adverbial or comparative).” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Genesis 18:4. The surrounding context includes family line.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מְעַט (H4592) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: מְעַט (mᵉʻaṭ) / H4592 is traced through Genesis 18:4, Genesis 24:17, Genesis 24:43, Genesis 26:10 with generated occurrence evidence.

definitions.short: a little or few (often adverbial or comparative)
definitions.usage: almost (some, very) few(-er, -est), lightly, little (while), (very) small (matter, thing), some, soon, × very.
